title: DODAG Configuration option (type 4) - all impls
notes: 2026-08-26 bounded three-implementation audit: NOT ready to claim/close. Python has no typed DODAG Configuration codec at all: python/src/lichen/rpl/messages.py carries type 4 only as generic RplOption bytes, and python/tests/rpl/test_messages.py:267 explicitly round-trips an invalid four-byte payload rather than enforcing RFC 6550's exact 14-byte data layout. Rust has typed DodagConfig in rust/lichen-rpl/src/message.rs:586-672 and rejects nonzero reserved data[10], preserving PCS/A/gateway flags. Zephyr C has a typed 14-byte parser/writer in lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/messages.c:264-327, but its struct omits PCS and A, parse ignores them, and parse accepts nonzero reserved data[10], so its semantic behavior differs from Rust. No DODAG Configuration case exists in canonical test/vectors/rpl_messages.json, no separate shared type-4 vector exists, and lichen/tests/rpl_dodag tests gateway behavior with manually constructed structs rather than byte-exact cross-language codec vectors. rust/lichen-rpl/src/lib.rs is currently shared dirty and excluded C/Zephyr changes are required, so isolated Python/Rust edits cannot complete acceptance. Leave open/unclaimed until one schema-backed canonical positive/negative corpus covers exact length, every field/flag, reserved bits/byte, bounds/trailing bytes and is consumed by production Python/Rust/C codecs. No files modified or tests run because source/vector inspection already demonstrates incompatible/missing consumers.
close_reason: Implemented exact type-4 DODAG Configuration parity across Python/Rust/Zephyr: typed Python codec/export, RFC A bit 3 and PCS preservation, gateway bit 7 extension, exact Data Length 14, reserved-bit/octet and writer-range rejection before output/state mutation, shared six-case corpus and independent consumers. Passed Python 91 tests; Rust vector and 3 unit tests plus Clippy in isolated target; C host vector and DODAG tests; pinned Zephyr v3.7 messages.c, dodag.c and app objects.
